sender.en: A “landlord” on Facebook Marketplace or a classifieds site

name.en: Fake rental: “send the deposit by e-Transfer to hold it”

how.en: A rental listing on social media or a classifieds site looks real, sometimes with photos copied from a real listing, a lease and land title documents. The “landlord” says they can’t show it yet, that many people are interested, and asks for a deposit or first month’s rent by e-Transfer to hold it. Once paid, they stop answering, and the place is not for rent or doesn’t exist.

text.en: You find a rental at a good price on Facebook Marketplace or a classifieds site.
The “landlord” is out of town or can’t show the place before you pay.
They say many people want it and you must send a deposit now.
You send a deposit or rent by e-Transfer and they disappear.

Hi, the apartment is still available but I have many people interested. I am working out of town so I can’t show it this week. Send the $1,200 deposit by e-Transfer today to hold it and I will send you the lease and keys.

en: landlord asked for deposit before viewing
sent first month's rent by e-transfer
You can’t see the unit before paying.
A landlord who is out of town or can’t meet.
Pressure: “first come, first served”, “send a deposit to hold it”.
Never send money before viewing the place in person.
Search the address and photos online for duplicate listings, and confirm who owns the property.
If you sent an e-Transfer, call your bank right away: it may be stopped if not yet accepted.
Report it to your local police and the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre, with screenshots of the ad and messages.
